Form tutor's note, Class 10B. Kishore Nair.
For two weeks Noor has struggled in the first three periods. She stares at the board, loses her place when reading aloud, and on Tuesday snapped at her lab partner, which isn't like her. By lunch she perks up. Today I asked her quietly after class whether mornings were hard. She said she has been skipping breakfast, partly to sleep longer and partly because "everyone says I've put on weight". She said it lightly, but she didn't look at me.
I told her there is nothing wrong with her body, and that a simple breakfast helps her brain work. I've asked her to meet the school counsellor this week, and I will call her mother tonight, privately, so they can talk and see the doctor if needed.

qa.a: Noor snapped at her lab partner.

qa.q: What does Noor's not looking at Kishore suggest about how she feels?
qa.a: It suggests Noor feels hurt and self-conscious about the comments on her weight, even though she spoke lightly.

qa.q: Which of Kishore's steps were wise?
qa.a: Kishore spoke privately, reassured Noor about her body, explained that breakfast helps her think, and arranged the counsellor and a private call home.

qa.q: How might Noor's mother feel after Kishore's call?
qa.a: Noor's mother may be worried, but glad to know early so she can talk with Noor gently and see the doctor if needed.

grounding: A teenager skips breakfast to sleep longer and to look thinner, feels foggy and moody before lunch, and an adult gently supports regular meals.

Monday, 9:15 pm
Today was a mess. I pressed snooze till 6:50, ran for the bus and skipped breakfast again. By third period my head felt stuffed with cotton. I read the same history paragraph four times and couldn't remember a word. When Anjali asked to borrow my eraser, I snapped at her for no reason. She looked hurt.
At break she held out half her poha. "You're always grumpy before lunch," she said. "You're just hungry." I ate it, a bit embarrassed. Twenty minutes later my brain came back online.
So here's the plan, written down so I stick to it: bread and a banana on the counter the night before, and an alarm with no snooze. Not a big deal, just something.
Also: say sorry to Anjali.
Ganga

qa.a: Anjali held out half her poha.

qa.q: How did Ganga feel after snapping at Anjali?
qa.a: Ganga felt embarrassed and a little guilty, and planned to say sorry.

qa.q: What simple plan did Ganga make?
qa.a: Bread and a banana on the counter the night before, and an alarm with no snooze.

qa.q: What might Anjali have felt when Ganga snapped?
qa.a: Anjali looked hurt, but still cared enough to share her poha and point out the hunger.
